stats.question: Does paved surface percent predict vacancy percent in apartment communities?
stats.method: OLS with HC3 robust standard errors
stats.interpretation: Across 40 buildings, each additional unit of paved surface (percentage points) is weakly and not significantly associated with 0.145 lower vacancy percent (95% CI -0.722 to 0.433, p=0.624), holding the controls fixed. This is an association, not a cause.
caveats: Observational association only; this does not show cause and effect.
Image measurements cover the Vexcel parcel or 80 m square, which may not match the whole community.

study.brief_markdown:
## Question
In Houston, do apartment communities with more paved surface have higher vacancy?

## Answer
No statistically significant relationship exists between paved surface area and vacancy rates in Houston apartment communities [E122].

## Method
The study sampled n = 40 [E1] multifamily apartment buildings in Houston market. Paved surface was measured as a percentage of approximately 80-meter square assessment areas around each address point using aerial image analysis [E122]. Vacancy rates were obtained from property records. A multiple regression model with OLS and HC3 robust standard errors estimated the association between paved surface percent and vacancy percent, controlling for building size (building_size_sq_ft), year built, total units, and building class [E122].

## Result
The regression coefficient for paved surface percent was -0.145 [E122] (95% CI: [-0.722, 0.433] [E122], p = 0.624 [E122]), indicating that each additional percentage point of paved surface was associated with 0.145 percentage points lower vacancy, though this relationship was not statistically significant. The r-squared was 0.161 [E122].

## Confidence and caveats
The study relies on observational data and association only; this does not demonstrate causation. While the sample size of n = 40 [E122] is adequate, the wide confidence interval and high p-value indicate substantial uncertainty in the relationship. Image measurements cover a small square around each address point, which may not represent the full community's surface composition. The two properties with extreme vacancy rates (63% [E122]) may represent exceptional cases (building distress or partial occupancy transitions) that complicate detection of underlying patterns.
caveats: Observational association only; this does not show cause and effect.
Image measurements cover the Vexcel parcel or 80 m square, which may not match the whole community.
